newsitem.title: GERMANY: Mannesmann off lows after 1997 outlook.
newsitem.headline: Mannesmann off lows after 1997 outlook.

text.p: Shares in German engineering group Mannesmann AG eased from their lows on Friday after the company issued a statement saying its earnings from ordinary activities would improve in 1997.
The shares had earlier come under selling pressure as dealers said a well-respected investment research house had downgraded the stock. However volumes were relatively limited, dealers noted.
Mannesmann shares were down 19 marks at 633 marks at 1203 GMT having earlier hit a low of 617 marks. The DAX index was down 0.2 percent at 3,342.72 points.
No confirmation was immediately available of the earlier downgrade.
"There were quite a few sales, especially from the U.K. side and then people moved to cover those when the Mannesmann statement came out," said a Frankfurt dealer.

Another dealer noted that some investors were shifting out of multi-industry companies with telecommunications interests into "purer" telecoms stocks -- primarily Deutsche Telekom AG amid fears that companies building up these divisions would face heavy start-up costs.
Several dealers also said there had been talk that Mannesmann was about to issue a profit warning.

In its statement, Mannesmann said its telecoms division would maintain its high earnings level of 1996 this year, and said it expected further earnings growth from its Mannesmann D2 mobile phone network.
